newsitem.title: ESTONIA: CENTRAL BANK SAYS ORDERS CREDIT RATING.
newsitem.headline: CENTRAL BANK SAYS ORDERS CREDIT RATING.

text.p: The Estonian central Bank said on Wednesday it has in principle decided to order a credit rating for Estonia and has begun technical preparations for it.
The central bank said in a statement that it hoped the move would help integrate Estonian financial markets and raise the efficiency of local financial intermediaries.
"The international integration of Estonia's financial markets is an important precondition for long-term and continuous economic growth," it added.
"The free movement of capital and an efficient financial sector enable an open economy to direct its productive means to spheres where earnings are the highest," it added.
Estonian banks have wanted a credit rating for some time as it would it easier for them to get funds from abroad.
Some commentators have said that a rating, expected to be good, would cause too many funds to arrive in Estonia and worsen what some see as an overheating economy.
Latvia and Lithuania already have ratings.
But the bank said that some of the problems that have delayed getting the credit rating still exist.
The bank said it was worried about delays in forming an effective legislative basis to maintain strong budget discipline.
Estonia's financial sector is also not using all the potential ways to maintain stable development, especially in macro-economic risks, it said.
"The central bank is therefore continuously ready to apply more stricter methods in monetary policy if guaranteeing balanced economic growth needs it," the bank added.
The bank also said that a rapid rise in credits and in the price of financial instruments was an example of factors that may cause it to apply stricter methods.
